div.head: ECf retr 38
div.ab: Quod nullus homo uiuum animal uel pannum usatum emeret siue aliud sine plegiis et bonis testibus, opusque aureum uel argenteum absque aurifabris uel monetariis. Prohibitum etiam erat in eadem lege, ne quis emeret uiuum animal uel pannum usatum sine plegiis et bonis testibus.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 668 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.
The bold opening, “Quod nullus homo … monetariis”, is the heading of the chapter in the Retractator.
The starred note (*) is printed under the ECf column; it is given here as well, since Lond is a manuscript of the Retractator.

div.ab: That no man should buy a living animal or used cloth or anything else without pledges and good witnesses, and work of gold or silver [not] without goldsmiths or moneyers. It was also prohibited in the same law that anyone should buy a living animal or used cloth without pledges and good witnesses.
